newsitem.title: USA: Nordstrom sees same-store sales up 2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nordstrom sees same-store sales up 2 pct.

text.p: Nordstrom Inc co-chairman John Whitacre said Monday the company is planning for comparable-store sales to rise two percent in the current holiday quarter over last year's levels.

In a conference call with analysts, monitored by Reuters, Whitacre noted that sales were relatively weak in last year's fourth quarter and said the apparel retailer has plenty of inventory to respond to stronger-than-expected sales.
Beyond the fourth quarter, which ends January 31, 1997, Nordstrom executives are planning for comparable-store sales to rise at an average rate of between 1.5 and two percent, Whitacre said.
So far this year comparable-store sales, which are closely watched by industry analysts, have risen 1.5 percent.

Executive vice president John Goesling said in the call that the company's board of directors next week will consider another stock repurchase program after a $100 million plan was completed this year.
"Certainly in my opinion we have the financial capacity to do more share repurchases, so if the board agrees with that we may be announcing another program," Goesling said.
Nordstrom plans to open three new department stores and several smaller stores next year, adding about 719,000 square feet of store space to its current total of 11.74 million, executives said.
Whitacre also said he thought the company had passed the "trough" of heavy price markdowns on certain of its apparel lines.
